title: Balak: the donkey saw first (Numbers 22:21–35)
hook: the donkey sees the angel before the famous prophet does
tomorrow: Balak: only the word I'm given

segments.voice: Yesterday, King Balak of Moab sent fees for divination to hire the seer Balaam to curse Israel. Your line was who's paying.

The dog won't go down the stairs. The toddler points at something in the corner of the room. The quiet intern says, I think the numbers are wrong. It's easy to brush them off; the experts are in charge. Balaam is the expert in this story, a seer a king will pay to see what others can't. He sets off on the road to Moab, riding his own donkey, the one he's ridden all his life. And on that road, the donkey sees something he doesn't.
screen: `THE DOG WON'T GO DOWN THE STAIRS.` → `THE HIRED SEER ON THE ROAD.` → `THE DONKEY SEES SOMETHING.`

segments.voice: In paraphrase: an angel of God stands in the road with a drawn sword. The donkey sees it and swerves into a field. Balaam beats her back onto the road. Then the path narrows between two vineyard walls. The angel stands there, and the donkey presses against the wall and crushes Balaam's foot. He beats her again. Then a place so narrow there's no way to turn at all. The donkey lies down under him, and Balaam, furious, beats her with his staff. Three times she saw. Three times he struck. Then God opens the donkey's mouth, and she asks, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?" Balaam answers her, as if talking donkeys were normal: you've made a fool of me; if I had a sword in my hand, I'd kill you. The rabbis enjoyed the irony. A man setting out to destroy a whole nation with his words can't handle his donkey without a sword. Then the donkey asks, gently: haven't I carried you all your life? Have I ever done this before? And he has to say no. Only then does God open Balaam's eyes, and he sees the angel. The Mishnah, in Pirkei Avot, lists the mouth of the donkey among ten things God created at twilight on the eve of the very first Sabbath, as if it had been waiting since creation for this one conversation. The hired seer saw last. The humble animal saw first, and the best thing it did was ask a question.
screen: `AN ANGEL WITH A DRAWN SWORD.` · `THREE TIMES SHE SAW, THREE TIMES HE STRUCK.` · `HAVE I EVER DONE THIS BEFORE?` · `TEN THINGS MADE AT TWILIGHT.`

segments.voice: Think of someone whose warnings you tend to wave away: a child, an older parent, a junior colleague, a friend who's usually quiet. Imagine them asking you the donkey's question, have I ever steered you wrong before, and let the answer come honestly.

Balak. The portion where a donkey sees the angel before the prophet does. And this week: the red heifer, Miriam's well, the rock, Aaron's death, the copper serpent, a hired curse, and now a donkey who saw first.
Your line: the donkey saw first. The humble one saw, and asked a question. Day four hundred sixty-two, done.

howItsDone: Balaam's talking donkey is read in synagogue in the portion of Balak, and it is often retold for children, with the donkey's question at the center.

original.note: Hebrew: she-donkey, the word used for Balaam's animal in Numbers 22.

trapdoor: what you thought: a funny story about a talking animal.
what it means: the famous seer is the last to see, and the humble animal asks the question that opens his eyes.

what a scholar hears: Avot 5:6 counts 'the mouth of the donkey' among ten things created at twilight before the first Sabbath; midrash mocks Balaam needing a sword for a donkey while cursing a nation with words.

chat.says: Why does the story let a donkey see more than the famous seer?
options: She saw the angel three times before he did; the humble one saw first.
The donkey was a prophet herself, sent to take over Balaam's job.
The angel hid behind a vineyard wall, where only the donkey could look.
chat.meaning: Three times the donkey saw the angel and turned aside; only after she spoke did God open Balaam's eyes.

Balaam.meaning: the seer hired to curse Israel

Moab.meaning: the kingdom of Balak, who hired Balaam

Mishnah.meaning: the early rabbis' collection of Jewish law and teaching

Pirkei Avot.meaning: chapters of the fathers, a book of the sages' sayings
